#2668. Payton Pritchard has to work through his struggles

Payton Pritchard has not yet met his own high standards this year.

His numbers are down across the board. He's dropped from 17 PPG on 46/38/89 splits last season to 13.4 PPG on 41/34/86, having one of the least efficient seasons of his career so far. Saturday's loss to the Kings was another rough night, and it came when Boston needed him most.

Pritchard went 4-for-17 from the field and 0-for-8 from three in his first start of the season. It's his fifth time shooting below 30% in 17 games.

With Jayson Tatum and Derrick White out, the expectation is that Pritchard takes on more of the scoring load. Struggling against Sacramento, which ranks 27th in defensive rating, is unusual. This is a matchup where you'd normally expect a big night. Instead, Boston got dragged into a dogfight that came down to the ball in his hands.

His final two shots showed where things went wrong. He hit a go-ahead jumper with 11 seconds left, then airballed at the buzzer with the game on the line.

With the floor cleared for him, he settled for a heavily contested step-back a foot inside the three-point line instead of attacking the rim. Pritchard didn't defend the shot afterward.

"Didn't get to a good enough spot," Pritchard said. "Probably need to try to find a better look there."

That was the bigger issue all night. Sacramento allows the highest field goal percentage at the rim in the league, a staggering 76.6%. Boston needed rim pressure, and Pritchard took just two shots there.

Even his 8-to-0 assist-to-turnover ratio is a bit misleading. One assist came when he tossed Neemias Queta a grenade late in the clock after failing to create space. There were several other occasions where he missed the roller, making his lack of turnovers more about being overly cautious.

He finished -13, the only Celtics starter in the negative. Plus-minus can be noisy in a single game, but this one matched the eye test. Meanwhile, his new mentor Mike Conley picked up the slack with a season-high 19 points and nearly saved the game.

It hasn't been all bad for Pritchard. But outside of two big games against the Bulls with 30 and 28 points, he hasn't been as advertised. Coming off a career year and a new contract extension, the expectation for him was another leap. So far it's looked closer to regression.

Pritchard didn't hide his own disappointment.

"As many good games as I'ma have, I have bad games, too," Pritchard said. "And tonight was a bad game. So, I look forward to bouncing back."

He usually finds his footing, and a couple of good games in a row can get him there. The Kings looked like a good launch pad. That wasn't the case, but there's a quick turnaround tonight against the Warriors, and a chance to wipe the slate clean

"It can either make you or break you," Pritchard said. "So go back to work and figure it out."

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

Las Vegas had a good chance to build some momentum out of halftime and couldn't capitalize.

#2660. Former Lakers $33 Million Signing Closing In on Deal With Division Rival

Former Los Angeles Lakers guard Gabe Vincent is reportedly closing in on a new NBA opportunity, and his next stop would put him in the same division as his former team.

Vincent, who signed a three-year, $33 million contract with the Lakers in 2023, is finalizing a deal with the Sacramento Kings, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.

The news comes after an extended stretch in free agency for the 30-year-old, whose Lakers tenure fell well short of expectations.

"Free agent guard Gabe Vincent is finalizing a deal with the Sacramento Kings, sources tell ESPN," Charania reported on November 22. "Vincent, 30, provides the Kings a veteran backup point guard behind rookie Darius Acuff Jr."

For Vincent, the reported agreement represents another opportunity to revive a career that looked considerably different when he first arrived in Los Angeles.

Vincent joined the Lakers in July 2023 after establishing himself as an important contributor during the Miami Heat's unexpected run to the NBA Finals.

#2659. Shai-Gilgeous Alexander, Giannis Antetokounmpo ruled out of Sunday's Thunder-Heat game

Sunday's game between the Oklahoma City Thunder and Miami Heat will be missing some serious star power.

The Heat ruled out Giannis Antetokounmpo out before tip-off with a groin injury. The missed game will be the first for Antetokounmpo since the former two-time MVP joined the Heat in the offseason.

The Thunder, meanwhile, ruled out reigning two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander with a lower back contusion and neck strain. The long-term outlook for both stars wasn't immediately clear. Both players started the day listed as questionable.

Antetokounmpo first surfaced on the injury report with his groin injury on Saturday before being ruled out on Sunday. It's not clear when he sustained it.

The Thunder are playing the first game of a back-to-back, but OKC head coach Mark Daigneault said pregame that the schedule didn't play a factor in the decision for Gilgeous-Alexander to sit. He cited "a really hard foul" of Gilgeous-Alexander in Friday's Thunder win over the Pelicans.

"It wouldn't be wise for us to put him on the court tonight regardless, based on how he's feeling," Daigneault said.

Gilgeous-Alexander joins a long list of injuries to critical Thunder players. Aday Mara (shin contusion), Alex Caruso (hip), Jaylin Williams (back) and Nikola Topić (hip) are also out against the Heat, joining Chet Holmgren (knee), Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jaylen Williams (ankle), who are all sidelined with long-term injuries.

The Thunder will start Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain, Micah Peavy, Kenrich Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein against the Heat. Bobby Portis Jr. will step into the starting lineup for Miami in place of Antetokounmpo.

Antetokounmpo and Gilgeous-Alexander are both playing at an All-NBA level this season. In 15 games, Antetokounmpo is averaging 28.2 points, 12.6 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 1.3 blocks while shooting 60.2% from the field. The Heat entered Sunday at 9-6, in sixth place in the East.

Gilgeous-Alexander is averaging 31.7 points, 4.5 assists and 4.1 rebounds through 16 games while shooting 48.3% from the floor and 37.3% from 3. The injury-ravaged Thunder entered Sunday at 10-6, in eighth place in the West.

#2658. MLB rumors: Blue Jays targeting Ketel Marte, Giants rejecting trade calls for ace Logan Webb

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The annual GM Meetings came and went this week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some sorely needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.

Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Saturday's hot stove happenings.

The Blue Jays have interest in Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte, who has a full no-trade protection, reports Sportsnet. It does not appear a trade is imminent. We ranked Marte among the offseason's top trade candidates despite his odd AWOL incidents the last few seasons. Even at 33, he remains one of the game's best second basemen.

The Blue Jays went 79-83 this past season largely because of their offense, which ranked dead last in runs and home runs. They also ranked 17th in WAR at second base as All-Star Ernie Clement ran out of steam in the second half. Offensively, Marte is coming off his worst 162-game season since 2018, though he would still represent a clear upgrade for the Blue Jays.

The Giants continue to decline trade calls about ace righty Logan Webb, reports USA Today. Webb, 30 next week, had his worst full season in the big leagues in 2026, in part due to a nagging knee injury, though he is signed affordably through 2028. San Francisco needs to add to its rotation, not subtract one of the game's best and most durable starters.

That said, a Webb trade would presumably net the Giants multiple young players and improve the team's talent base. It never hurts to listen, but for now, the Giants seem disinclined to move their best pitcher since Madison Bumgarner was in his prime. Webb and Landen Roupp are the only locks for San Francisco's 2027 rotation at the moment.

Not surprisingly, the Braves want to add at least one starting pitcher, according to The Athletic. They could also re-sign Raisel Iglesias or bring in another late-inning reliever even after signing Phillips. Chris Sale and Grant Holmes are Atlanta's only returning healthy starters. Bryce Elder (knee), Spencer Schwellenbach (elbow) and Spencer Strider (elbow) all finished the season injured.

The Braves will give Didier Fuentes, who was so dominant as a reliever this past season, a chance to start in 2027. It will be difficult to count on him for a full season, however. Fuentes, 21, threw a career-high 97 innings between the minors, majors, and postseason in 2026. Atlanta will need to monitor his workload next year. Another starter to soak up innings is a must this offseason.

The Tigers have interest in free agent left-hander Shota Imanaga, reports MLB.com. Jackson Jobe, Troy Melton, River Ryan, and Framber Valdez are presumably locks for Detroit's rotation. Ty Madden and Keider Montero are depth options. Reese Olson is expected back from shoulder surgery early next year. Still, the Tigers could clearly use another starting pitcher.

We ranked Imanaga, 33, as the 30th-best free agent available this offseason. He has been very home run prone the last two years (1.9 homers per nine innings), which could make him a good match for what is now called Fifth Third Park. Detroit's stadium tends to play pitcher-friendly, particularly in April and September (and October), when the ball doesn't carry well in the cold.

The Blue Jays are receiving calls about infielder Ernie Clement and utility man Davis Schneider, reports The Athletic. Teams have also inquired about catcher Brandon Valenzuela, who was a Gold Glove finalist as a rookie in 2026. Toronto reportedly has interest in Jazz Chisholm Jr. as it seeks more of a power bat on the infield, potentially making Clement expendable.

Schneider, 27, had a poor 2026 and spent time in Triple-A, though he is versatile and has hit lefties in spots over the years. There is a shocking shortage of quality right-handed bats throughout baseball right now. Schneider's heavy plate discipline approach and ability to play left field as well as some infield positions make him an interesting enough target this offseason.

The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox are among several teams pursuing Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the San Diego Union-Tribune. Taira, 26, had a 1.36 ERA in 145 innings for the Seibu Lions in 2026. We ranked him as the 19th-best free agent available this offseason, though he could ultimately wind up in the bullpen given his height (5-foot-8).

The Padres and two Chicago teams need starting pitching this offseason (they need multiple starters, really) and would likely use Taira in their rotation, at least to begin the season. For what it's worth, Taira told Sanspo he does not have a preferred destination, geographically. The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox would all give him a chance to pitch for a contender right away.

The Cardinals have declined trade inquiries into first baseman Alec Burleson and shortstop Masyn Winn, according to the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. St. Louis is also receiving interest in catchers Jimmy Crooks and Pedro Pagés, who are more likely to be traded. Burleson and Winn are off-limits, though, and considered part of the long-term future in St. Louis.

Leo Bernal, who was so impressive during his September call up, and top prospect Rainiel Rodriguez are the future behind the plate for the Cardinals. Pagés is a traditional glove-first backup catcher. Crooks has some offensive upside thanks to his hard-hit ability (exit velocity, etc.), and he rates well as a pitch-framer and thrower. He's an appealing target for catcher-needy teams.

#2655. Cowboys open game with 6 straight touchdowns, rip Titans in Dallas

The Dallas Cowboys did not have the worst defense on the field for a game this season, but the story Sunday was their offense.

The Cowboys showed some improved defensive execution in Sunday's 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans, although it was mostly in comparison to their opponent's defense. Dallas scored touchdowns on its first six offensive possessions of the game and scored on their first eight series in the blowout at AT&T Field.

The only failures: A Brandon Aubrey field goal and the Cowboys kneeling down to end the game.

Dak Prescott was nearly perfect against the Titans' harried defense, throwing for 325 yards and four TDs and rushing for another score. Prescott's rushing score gave the Cowboys their sixth TD in as many possessions.

It was Prescott's second straight game accounting for five TDs. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both caught TD passes, and Javonte Williams had one score each receiving and rushing.

Dallas' shortest drive before the fourth quarter was 56 yards. A Titans defense that saw multiple starters dealt prior to the trade deadline had little chance to slowing down the Cowboys.

The Cowboys (5-6) stayed within range of the first-place New York Giants (5-3-1) in the NFC East. The Titans dropped to 1-9, still in line to earn the top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft as of now.

Dallas' incremental improvements defensively Sunday came with caveats, including Carnell Tate's 59-yard touchdown reception in which four Cowboys defenders failed to touch Tate while he was down.

Another hiccup was allowing ex-Cowboys running back Tony Pollard to run for 110 yards, at 5.2 yards per clip. There were also some costly penalties on the Cowboys' defense, which made a play-calling change from Christian Parker to Mike Pettine.

But there were positives. Dallas sacked Cam Ward five times, including a strip sack, and held the Titans to 112 first-half yards while building a three-score lead.

The Cowboys came out aggressively, winning the coin flip and opting to take the ball first. After converting a fourth-and-2 from inside the Tennessee 5-yard line, Williams punched it in for the first score. Dallas went for 2 and failed.

The Titans kicked the first of three first-half field goals to cut the lead in half, but the Cowboys struck back on KaVontae Turpin's 22-yard rushing score.

Dallas got the ball back and chewed up more than six minutes on its next TD drive, capped by Prescott hitting Lamb on a gorgeous throw in the back of the end zone.

The Titans settled for two more field goals to close out the first half. Prescott's TD pass to Pickens made it 27-9, Dallas, at halftime.

Ward called his own number on an audible on the Titans' opening drive, sneaking it in for a rushing touchdown on Tennessee's opening drive of the second half. But the Titans never made it less than a two-score game the rest of the way.

The Cowboys beat the Titans 51-30 on Sunday. This final score is what is colloquially known as Scorigami, meaning that it is the first time this final score has occurred in NFL history.

Tennessee went down fighting. With 31 seconds left in the game, quarterback Cam Ward found Calvin Ridley for the 12-yard score.

The Titans scored 30 points, but it will not be enough after the impressive display the Cowboys put on today.

The Cowboys offense has dropped a 50-burger.

After the long fumble recovery, Dallas needed just three plays for paydirt. Cowboys tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford caught Dak Prescott's fourth touchdown pass of the game, this one for two yards.

The Cowboys now lead 51-23 with just under five minutes to go.

The Dallas defense finally had a big play to go along with how dominant the offense has been today.

Quinnen Williams obliterated Cam Ward from the blind side and the Titans quarterback fumbled it.

The ball bounces around, before a Cowboys corner finally picks it up and runs it 70 yards, flipping the field.

The Cowboys have finally gone a drive without scoring a TD. Dallas previously was 6-for-6 scoring a touchdown on each of its six drives to open the game against Tennessee.

Finally, the Titans defense kept the Cowboys out of the end zone.

Instead, Brandon Aubrey nailed the 49-yard field goal.

Dallas now leads 44-23 with 11:33 left to go in the game.

Tennessee watched as Dallas scored its sixth touchdown on as many drives. The Titans got a first down, but then had two incompletions, a sack and a delay of game.

This resulted in Tennessee choosing to punt down 41-23 with 2 minutes left in the third quarter.

The Cowboys offense has been perfect against the Titans. Dallas has had the ball six times and has scored six touchdowns.

The most recent came from Dak Prescott keeping the ball. He ran to the right and scored the 2-yard touchdown. Prescott just broke the plane of the goal line and the score was confirmed.

Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate had a wild 59-yard touchdown against Dallas.

Tate went to the ground, but managed to get his body off the ground by the time the Cowboys defenders got to him. The rookie was touched by Dallas defenders, but since he was off the ground, he took off for the end zone after the defense left him alone.

Tate scored the TD, and the play was reviewed nd he was confirmed to be off the ground when touched.

Dallas has had the ball five times against Tennessee, and has now scored five touchdowns.

Javonte Williams scored his second of the day as he took a pass from Dak Prescott 11 yards for the score.

Tennessee's offense got the break it needed during halftime. The Titans ran only four plays and benefited from a 38-yard DPI call.

Regardless, on first and goal from the 1, Cam Ward dove for the end zone after taking the snap and broke the plane of the end zone for the score.

The Cowboys take a 27-9 lead into halftime.

Tennessee's offense got down the field, but simply ran out of time. Cam Ward spiked the ball with 1-second left on the clock.

This set up a 28-yard field goal for Joey Slye, which he made. Slye has all of the Titans' points so far, with three field goal makes.

Dallas' Big 3 has each found the end zone now. After Javonte Williams and CeeDee Lamb had already scored, George Pickens finally got his.

Dak Prescott threw the ball over the middle and found Pickens for the 10-yard score.

Dallas' defensive strategy may just be to score a TD on every possession and hope that is enough. Currently, on Sunday, it is as the Cowboys lead 27-6 with just over four minutes left in the first half.

Tennessee ran six plays and picked up only 18 yards, but it was enough to get into field goal range.

Titans running back Tony Pollard picked up 19 yards on three carries, but a sack and an incompletion brought up fourth-and-eight on the Dallas 30.

Joey Slye came out for the 48-yard field goal attempt and nailed it. Tennessee trails 20-6 with 10:34 left in the first half.

It looked like Dak Prescott was throwing the ball away under pressure from the Tennessee defense.

Prescott was rolling right and just barely got the pass off. It looked destined for out of bounds, but then CeeDee Lamb came into frame and the pass was perfectly placed for Lamb to not only grab it, but also get the necessary two feet in for the score.

Tennessee's offense was clicking on its first possession of the game, but not the second.

The Titans had a five-yard run on first down, lost a yard on a Carnell Tate reeption on second down and then Cam Ward was sacked by Justin Houston on third down.

The quarter ended, but when the second quarter starts, the Titans will be punting.

While the Dallas defense has struggled, the offense is firing on all cylinders. The Cowboys picked up 74 yards on six plays, including a touchdown run by wide receiver KaVontae Turpin.

The speedster showed off his wheels and went around the left end for a 22-yard score.

Dallas didn't go for 2 this time and just let Brandon Aubrey knock through the extra point. The Cowboys lead 13-3.

One of the main stories this week was Dallas DC Christian Parker losing play-calling duties to Mike Pettine while remaining the DC.

Dallas' defense went with a bend-don't-break approach on Tennessee's first drive of the game.

Cam Ward hit Chimere Dike for a 22-yard gain, then later had an 8-yard reception. Running back Tony Pollard picked up 13 on a carry.

The Titans got into the redzone but were unable to find the end zone. Instead, Joey Slye knocked through a 38-yard field goal to make it 6-3, with the Cowboys in front.

Tennessee's challenge of the first down was not successful.

Dallas got the fresh set of downs and ran Javonte Williams twice. On the second attempt, the running back forced his way into the end zone for the score.

The Cowboys opted to go for two because of a penalty giving them a closer attempt, but it failed.

Dallas has been grooving its way down the field against Tennessee.

Facing fourth and short, the Cowboys kept the offense on the field and went for it. Quarterback Dak Prescott kept the ball for a quarterback keeper, and it looked on the broadcast that he had easily gotten it.

Tennessee head coach Robert Saleh wasn't convinced, though, and tossed an early challenge flag. The ruling was upheld — first down, Cowboys.

Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate will return to the active lineup for Tennessee in Week 11, officially active for the first time since Week 7 after dealing with a shoulder injury.

Despite having missed two games, Tate leads the team with 413 receiving yards this year with a single receiving touchdown. His presence will be key this week, especially after teammate Wan'Dale Robinson was placed on season-ending injured reserve with an ankle injury this week.

Here's a look at the full list of inactives for Titans-Cowboys in Week 11.

#2653. JJ Redick non-committal on Austin Reaves’ potential injury return vs. Jazz

JJ Redick non-committal on Austin Reaves' potential injury return vs. Jazz appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Lakers have one home game remaining on their current four-game stand, before they head out on a four-game road trip that will carry them through the start of December. And it's possible that the Lakers get star guard Austin Reaves back in the lineup as he rehabs from a heel injury.

Following Lakers' practice on Sunday, head coach JJ Redick acknowledged that Austin Reaves was a full participant in practice, although the team did not do any live work. He has progressed in his recovery, although Redick stopped short of saying he would potentially be available for the team's game against the Utah Jazz on Monday.

"They're doing a great job of figuring out the most comfortable insert and the most comfortable shoe, finding that right combination," Redick said. "I had one, mine was in a different spot. Mine was on the bottom of my heel. Did it when I played for the Clippers in the last regular season game and had to go play with it in the playoffs … it was super painful. His is in a different spot, it's on the medial side so it's kind of on the bottom of the foot. But it's really just a comfort issue, and it's getting better every day."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Lakers have gone 3-1 in the most recent stretch of games that Reaves has missed, and Redick admitted that the increased shot creation and usage that has fallen on Luka Doncic in his absence has taken a toll on the Slovenian star.

While Redick has seen an improvement in the team's defense, and he credits that to being a big reason why the Lakers' have stayed afloat in Reaves' absence, the reality is they've struggled more in terms of half-court offense. That's the main area where Reaves' presence helps the team.

"The reality is we're shooting significantly less at the rim. I compared the percentage. We're less efficient on non-rim paint twos and we're shooting less efficiently from three. So we're missing shots, Luka's had three high-turnover games this week. But the stat that stands out the most is for 12 games, we were the number one half-court offense. Austin as on the court for 70 percent of those possessions," Redick said.

"In the last seven games, we've not been a good half-court offense, Austin has been on the court in 9 percent of those. So who would have thought that not having an elite offensive player, All-Star level player would hurt your offense? … We're gonna be fine."

Reaves has officially been diagnosed with a heel bruise. The injury occurred during the Lakers' win against the Milwaukee Bucks on Nov. 11 when he went up for a breakaway dunk attempt and landed awkwardly. Redick has already confirmed that there is no structural damage, it's simply about pain management.

The six-year veteran guard had appeared in 12 games prior to the injury, at a little over 35 minutes per game. He was averaging 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals while shooting 51.3 percent from the field, 40.9 percent from the 3-point line and 91.5 percent from the free-throw line.

Should Reaves not be able to play against the Jazz this coming Monday, the next opportunity he would have to rejoin the lineup would be Friday, Nov. 27 on the road against the San Antonio Spurs in the Lakers' final NBA Cup game.

The Las Vegas Raiders and Denver Broncos will face off for the first time this season in Week 11's afternoon window, with kickoff set for 4:25 p.m. ET at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver.

After starting the season 3-0, the Raiders have been on a slide, going 1-6 over their past seven games. No. 1 overall pick rookie Fernando Mendoza is set to make his second career start following the trade of Kirk Cousins ahead of the deadline this week, up against another challenging defense after facing the Seattle Seahawks in Week 11. All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers is inactive for this matchup, leaving Mendoza without his top receiving option.

The Broncos entered the week tied with the Kansas City Chiefs for the best record in the AFC West at 7-2. They're 10.5-point home favorites in this contest and are on a five-game winning streak coming off the Week 10 bye. That win streak began as head coach Sean Payton resumed offensive play-calling from OC Davis Webb after a slow start on offense.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Raiders face the Broncos in Week 11, airing on CBS.

Las Vegas had a good chance to build some momentum out of halftime and couldn't capitalize.

The Raiders picked up eight yards on three plays and opted to punt.

Klint Kubiak's interview heading into halftime was brief.

He was asked how the Raiders turn it around after two turnovers and 7 penalties in the first half.

Kubiak said, "They need to call it both ways," and went to the locker room.

Bo Nix and the Broncos were out of field goal range and didn't want the Raiders to get another offensive position. Rather than just kneel out the half, Nix took a shot toward the end zone.

Las Vegas picked it off, though the first half was over.

Denver leads 17-10. Las Vegas gets the ball out of halftime.

Fernando Mendoza scored the first touchdown of his career last week, and it was a rushing score.

Mendoza finally notched his first passing touchdown. It was a nice pass to Ashton Jeanty who broke a tackle and took it 68 yards for the score.

Denver was forced to put after Bo Nix was sacked on third down. Denver had it third and two, but Nix was almost instantly under pressure, and he was sacked for a loss of seven yards.

The Raiders offense finally showed life thanks to a huge run by Ashton Jeanty.

It looked like Las Vegas even had a touchdown, but it was called back for offensive pass interference. The Raiders weren't able to recover and had to settle for a 28-yard field goal.

Denver leads 17-3 with 6:43 left to go in the first half.

The Raiders star running back looked like he did playing for Boise State. He broke off a 46-yard run, helping Las Vegas find some much needed offensive momentum.

Broncos ran a flea-flicker trick play and picked up 36 yards as Bo Nix found Marvin Mims Jr.

Mims was ruled down just short of the end zone, though and Denver was forced to run more plays to try and score. After Bo Nix was stuffed on first down, Jonah Coleman bulldozed his way into the end zone for the score.

Las Vegas cannot get anything going on offense. Through three drives, the Raiders have 21 yards of offense and have punted three times.

The most recent drive was two incompletions and a no-yard rush for Ashton Jeanty.

Denver head coach Sean Payton has always loved thight ends.

Payton showed why when the Broncos were on the 1-yard line. Bo Nix found Adam Trautman to the left for the 1-yard score.

Denver leads 10-0 early in the second quarter.

The Raiders were facing third and 28. Las Vegas opted to give Ashton Jeanty a carry and he picked up six.

The Raiders punted it back to Denver after running four plays and generating just two yards.

Ashton Jeanty picked up three yards on Las Vegas' first play of the first drive. Fernando Mendoza had an incompletion on second down and then lost track of the play clock causing Klint Kubiak to burn an early timeout.

Mendoza then found Jeanty for a gain of 6 on third down.

The Raiders looked like they were going to punt, but the Broncos blocked it and took over with phenomenal field position.

After Denver converted its first 3rd and 10+ of the season, Denver had a 3-yard run and then back-to-back incompletions.

The Broncos elected to put and Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders offense will take the field for the first time today.

Denver came into this week as the only team in the league that hadn't converted a third-down conversion of at least ten yards.

It doesn't sound bad if maybe the team just didn't have many attempts from that far.

Facing third and 12, though, Bo Nix found Pat Bryant for the 21-yard gain, as the Broncos converted their first 3rd-and-10+ conversion of the year.

#2649. Bears Making Super Bowl Push Amid Uncertain Future

CHICAGO—These are highly consequential times for the Bears, as they make a potential Super Bowl push in a season that's playing out against the backdrop of their new stadium deliberations and a prospective mega-deal for third-year quarterback Caleb Williams this offseason.

Those elements came together on a gray, occasionally rainy, but mild Sunday at Soldier Field. The Bears may be working on finding their next home, but they're also still busy trying to generate a few lasting memories in their venerable, old one. They extended their winning streak to five games and remained in the thick of the Super Bowl-contending mix in the NFC by beating the Saints, 21–13.

This is a flagship NFL franchise. But the Bears' on-field glories are ever-more-distant memories. They last reached the Super Bowl in the 2006 season, losing the big game then to Peyton Manning and the Colts with a team that had Lovie Smith as its coach and Rex Grossman as its quarterback. The Bears last won the Super Bowl after the 1985 season with the memorably dominant team of Mike Ditka, Walter Payton, Jim McMahon, an all-time-great defense, and the "Super Bowl Shuffle" bravado.

"We're due for one," an Uber driver said Sunday while en route to Soldier Field.

The parking lots by the stadium were relatively filled even more than three hours before the noon local time kickoff. Fans displayed huge Bears flags above their tailgating locations. It was a relatively warm weekend, with people still wearing shorts Saturday night with temperatures in the 60s on the day of the Magnificent Mile Lights Festival and holiday parade. The members of the Chicago Bears Drumline practiced on the field a few hours ahead of Sunday's kickoff.

Chants of "Let's go Bears! Let's go Bears!" rang out from the crowd of 59,911 during the fourth quarter. Practically no one, it seemed, exited early to beat the postgame traffic.

The number of such Sunday afternoon experiences at Soldier Field is beginning to dwindle, but the site of the Bears' next stadium remains undetermined. The fall veto session for the Illinois legislature runs through Dec. 3. Legislators are finalizing a new stadium proposal designed to keep the team in the state, rather than having the Bears leave for a competing stadium proposal in northwest Indiana that's legislatively approved.

"We expect productive dialogue with both leadership teams in the coming weeks," the Bears said earlier this month. "We have a responsibility and obligation to explore every option available to the club."

The newest legislation in Illinois includes the creation of a municipal stadium authority that would own a new domed stadium. The Bears would fund the stadium construction. About $855 million in public money would go toward infrastructure costs, such as new roads around the venue.

A meeting last month involving NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker helped to reopen the conversations. That meeting occurred as the Bears contemplated a potential move to Hammond, Indiana. State leaders there already have approved a funding package for a new stadium. Bears president Kevin Warren said in August that Hammond was the team's "sole focus" in its stadium site search.

The franchise's stadium deliberations in Illinois have focused on land that it owns in suburban Arlington Heights.

There also is pending business to be conducted with Williams, the quarterback chosen first overall in the 2024 NFL Draft out of USC. He becomes eligible for a contract extension this offseason, under the provisions of the NFL's rookie compensation system. Some observers wonder whether he and other members of the celebrated 2024 draft class of quarterbacks will get top-of-the-market money.

That could mean a deal approaching or even surpassing an average of $70 million per season for Williams, who does not have an NFL Players Association-certified agent but has a representation team led by his father Carl.

"Back up the Brinks truck," broadcaster and former NFL safety Ryan Clark told Front Office Sports editor-in-chief Daniel Roberts last week. " … Let's give him his money."

For now, the Bears have the luxury of trying to construct a Super Bowl team around a quarterback still on his comparatively inexpensive rookie contract. Williams originally signed a four-year deal with the Bears worth a guaranteed $39.49 million. He is making about $4.3 million in salary and bonuses this season while counting approximately $10.7 million against the Bears' salary cap, including the prorated amount of his original signing bonus. He is set to make about $6 million next season and count approximately $12.5 million against the cap.

NFL success is all about having a capable coach-and-quarterback combination. Williams and the Bears thrived last season after the franchise's hiring of Ben Johnson as its coach. The Bears are paying Johnson an estimated $13 million per season, a considerable amount for a first-time NFL head coach but not quite at the top of a pay scale that's now around $20 million annually for some coaches.

Johnson and Williams got the Bears to the divisional round of last season's NFC playoffs. They could go even further this season. They added star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons ahead of this month's NFL's trade deadline. Sunday's win improved the Bears' record to 8–2, keeping them in a virtual tie for first place in the ultra-competitive NFC North division race.

"We win in multiple ways," Williams said after the game. "And that's good for us as a team to know that when we get in these situations throughout the year and late this year … we know that we can win in multiple ways."

"He's a momentum-changer," Williams said. "He swings momentum in our favor a lot of times."

A Super Bowl appearance in February in Los Angeles is far from certain. But it clearly is possible. Next, the Bears have a quick turnaround for a big Thanksgiving Day matchup with the Lions in Detroit.

"Every game counts as one," Johnson said. "But this one, because it's a divisional one, you can say it's one and a half. You know, it's a big one. … We'll be able to catch up on rest after Thursday. But the next little bit is gonna be a race to get ready for this next one."

#2648. What's next for Red Sox after Jake Bauers deal? Plus more intel from the MLB GM Meetings

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

LAS VEGAS — Uncertainty permeated the ARIA Resort & Casino throughout this week's MLB GM Meetings. The looming lockout, of course, played a major role in all of this.

With Dec. 1  approaching, media, executives, and all within the baseball industry had some questions: what would baseball look like once the inevitable lockout goes into place? What will it look like once it returns? How do you build a roster with such indeterminacy?

For the Red Sox, a small piece of this peculiar period centers on what to do with former top prospect Kristian Campbell.

Tuesday (Nov. 17) is a significant date, marking the deadline for teams to decide which players to protect from the Rule 5 draft by adding them to their 40-man roster. Campbell, who did not appear in a big-league game in 2026, is currently on the 40-man, signing an eight-year $60 million extension just eight games into his 2025 rookie campaign. But after his demotion in late June of that season, Campbell never found his way back to the majors.

Now, with the lockout upon baseball, according to one source familiar with the situation, Campbell's 40-man spot might be in jeopardy.

Boston is weighing the possibility of designating Campbell for assignment. When Craig Breslow, the Sox's president of baseball operations, was asked about that Tuesday, he brushed aside the question.

"I'm not going to speak to that right now," he said "Kristian's part of our organization. We're really happy about that, and we are invested in doing everything we can to get him to perform like he's capable of."

Now, if the Red Sox do DFA Campbell, the belief is that he would clear waivers, given his contract and lackluster performance at the minor-league level. Campbell is owed $55 million over the next six seasons, earning $13 million and $16 million over the 2031 and 2032 seasons, respectively. Campbell posted a .256/.383/.380 slash line with eight homers in 462 plate appearances at Triple-A in 2026.

Because of those figures, one league executive suggested during the GM Meetings that their club would have no interest in Campbell. The exec took it a step further, confidently suggesting that they couldn't envision any team claiming the outfielder, considering the contract.

Hypothetically, if Campbell is DFA'd, the Red Sox would free up a 40-man roster spot. If he clears waivers, Campbell, who has less than a year of MLB service time, would be outrighted to Triple-A Worcester. The Red Sox could then eventually add him back to the 40-man roster once they feel his production is worthy of another promotion to the parent club.

None of this would provide the Red Sox with any financial relief unless another team were to claim him. Campbell's contract would still count toward their competitive balance tax payroll even if he were removed from the 40-man roster and remained in the minors.

The risk-reward of such a move is something the Red Sox will also have to consider. Campbell has already acknowledged losing confidence following his recent struggles at both the major- and minor-league levels.

"He's got a world of potential," said Breslow. "We saw it in the minor leagues when he was coming up. We saw it in the first part of the season in [2025]. Then I think we started to see it in the second half last year, too, [at Worcester]. I still feel like he has a really bright big-league career ahead of him, and excited to get into spring training and see that manifest on the field."

The Red Sox signed Jake Bauers to a four-year, $58 million deal Friday, giving the club another power bat in their lineup. Willson Contreras will continue to anchor first base while Bauers will serve as the primary DH, filling in for Contreras from time to time.

Bauers had a breakout season with the Brewers this year, batting .266/.389/.484 with an .874 OPS and 26 homers. The combo of plate discipline and damage in the strike zone intrigued the Red Sox. Furthermore, his ability to lift the ball in the air and use the entire field despite being a lefty gives the Red Sox confidence that he will be productive at Fenway.

With Bauers part of the fold, though, Jarren Duran's future with the club is even more murky. The Sox are a heavily left-handed offensive club with Bauers, Wilyer Abreu, Masataka Yoshida, Roman Anthony, and Duran in the mix.

One is likely going to have to go. And Duran, who could earn upwards of $11 million in arbitration next season, appears to be the most likely to be dealt.

Even before the Bauers signing, multiple sources suggested during the GM Meetings that both the Red Sox and Duran might be better off parting ways via trade.

"I've been hearing for three years now about the outfield logjam that we have, but the reality is we haven't had all of our outfielders, including Masataka, healthy at the same time," Breslow said. "These things have largely taken care of themselves, unfortunately."

Giants head coach John Harbaugh is showing he trusts his rookie kicker.

New York drove the field against the Jacksonville defense.

New York leads 10-6 early in the second quarter.

New York was on the goal line and gave it to Cam Skattebo to try to get the touchdown on third down.

Bhayshul Tuten was back in the game for Jacksonville and seems to be fine.

New York ends its first drive with a punt.

#2642. Alexander-Walker has 27 points as Hawks roll to 107-97 win over Pistons in off game for Cunningham

ATLANTA (AP) — Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 27 points, Atlanta opened the fourth quarter with an 18-0 run, and the Hawks beat the Detroit Pistons 107-97 on Sunday as Cade Cunningham was held to a season-low five points.

Cunningham set a season high with 15 assists but a combination of early foul trouble and a sore knee combined to hold him to 20 points below his average of 25.6 as he made 2 of 9 shots. It was his first game of the season not scoring in double figures.

Corey Kispert scored a season-high 18 points and Lu Dort had 16 in the Hawks' fourth straight win.

Isaiah Joe led Detroit with 19 points. Ausar Thompson and John Collins had 18 and Paul Reed added 16.

The Pistons led 85-74 at the start of the fourth quarter before the Hawks took a 92-85 with the 18 unanswered points. Joe's 3-pointer with 4:52 remaining ended Detroit's scoreless streak.

Cunningham picked up two fouls in the first period and was called for his third foul early in the second. He was limited to 14 minutes in the first half while missing all three of his shots from the field.

Cunningham scored his first points with a jumper off the glass early in the second half but continued to focus on setting up shots for teammates while receiving extra defensive attention from Dyson Daniels and the Hawks.

Cunningham was included on Detroit's injury report with right knee soreness. Coach J.B. Bickerstaff said before the game protecting Cunningham was "the most important thing. He's a competitor and wants to play. But it's also our responsibility to just make sure that we're protecting him at all costs."

Cunningham was held out of Detroit's 122-109 win at New Orleans on Wednesday night but scored 23 points in a 105-102 loss to Toronto on Friday night.

Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings had 10 points after missing three games with a sore back.

Pistons: Play at Orlando on Tuesday night.

#2641. Why Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence has legitimate 2026 NFL MVP case, is destined to win one at some point

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Trevor Lawrence has spent the past 17 regular-season games building an MVP résumé. On Sunday against the Giants (4:25 p.m., CBS and live streaming on Paramount+), the Jaguars quarterback gets another opportunity to show why his candidacy deserves more attention.

Yes, it may be weird to read the words "NFL MVP candidate" next to the Jaguars' quarterback, which is understandable. Jacksonville is the only current franchise in the league that has never had a player receive a first-place MVP vote. However, Lawrence is performing like an MVP-caliber quarterback for a Jaguars team whose 7-2 record is tied for the next-best record in the NFL, behind only the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers and the 8-1 Buffalo Bills. It's just the third time in franchise history the Jaguars have started 7-2 or better through their first nine games, and the first time since 1999, according to Stathead. Among qualified quarterbacks, Lawrence ranks top-five in the league in pass yards per attempt, passing touchdowns, passer rating, success rate and EPA (expected points added) per dropback, plus a top-10 finish in touchdown-to-interception ratio and completion percentage, per NFL Next Gen Stats.

That's why DraftKings Sportsbook is giving him the fourth-best odds (+550) to take home the NFL MVP hardware entering Week 11. The only three players with better odds are Joe Burrow (-125), Josh Allen (+370), and Brock Purdy (+450). However, Lawrence is also racking up eye-popping numbers in an offense without any other established NFL stars, unlike the three quarterbacks ahead of him. Burrow has Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins at wide receiver, plus four-time Pro Bowler Orlando Brown Jr. at left tackle. Allen has 2025 NFL rushing champion James Cook at running back and five-time Pro Bowler Dion Dawkins at left tackle. Purdy has 2023 NFL Offensive Player of the Year Christian McCaffrey at running back, plus George Kittle and Trent Williams.

Close your eyes and think. Who is the most accomplished Jacksonville offensive player outside of Lawrence? Running back Bhayshul Tuten is in just his second NFL season and his first as a lead back. No. 1 wide receiver Parker Washington, a 2023 sixth-round pick, is in his fourth NFL season and has never recorded a 1,000-yard receiving season -- he is well on pace to do so for the first time in 2026 with 645 yards receiving in the first 9 games of the year, which ranks 16th in the league. None of his offensive linemen have ever earned a Pro Bowl selection. Lawrence is uplifting a cast of solid, budding young talent and producing at an elite level similar to, or better than in some metrics, the other quarterbacks up for NFL MVP through 10 weeks.

This first-half performance in 2026 isn't a fluke either. Once Lawrence adjusted to coach Liam Coen's scheme halfway through 2025, their first season together, he led the entire NFL in total touchdowns with 24 across the last eight games of the 2025 regular season, a span in which Jacksonville went a perfect 8-0 to finish 13-4 and win the AFC South. Lawrence's 38 total touchdowns ranked as the third-most in football last season behind only the league's last two MVP winners: Matthew Stafford (46) and Josh Allen (39). That's how he finished fifth in 2025 NFL MVP voting, behind only Stafford, Drake Maye, Allen and McCaffrey last season.

Across the final six games of the 2025 season, Lawrence produced a ridiculous 19 total touchdowns to just one turnover. That feat made him just the third player in NFL history to record 19-plus total touchdowns and one or fewer turnovers in the final six games of a season. The other two players to do so are 2019 Drew Brees (20 total touchdowns to one turnover) and 2020 NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers (21 total touchdowns to one turnover). Combining the second half of last season and the first half of this season, Lawrence has 15 wins and 45 total touchdowns in his last 17 regular-season games. He's been one of the NFL's best for the last year's worth of regular-season games.

How rare is 15-plus wins and 45-plus total touchdowns in a 17-game span? According to CBS Sports Research, Lawrence is just the 10th quarterback in league history to do it, and the previous 9 all won NFL MVP honors at some point in their storied careers.

15-plus wins and 45-plus TDs in a 17-game span, NFL history

* All won NFL MVP in their career besides Lawrence

It will likely take Lawrence repeating his second-half effort from 2025 once again in 2026 to swipe the league MVP award out of Burrow's hands, but there's a chance he could do just that. If 2026 isn't the year Lawrence takes home NFL MVP honors, it's coming in the not-so-distant future.

#2640. 10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This Friday, Nov. 20, is an important date on MLB's offseason calendar. It is the deadline for teams to offer 2027 contracts to their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players. The player does not have to sign by Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline, but he must be offered a contract. If he's not, the player is considered non-tendered and immediately becomes a free agent.

Dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary. Adolis García, Nathaniel Lowe, Alek Manoah, and Christopher Morel were among the notable non-tenders last offseason. Go back a few years and big names like Cody Bellinger and Kyle Schwarber were non-tendered.

With that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors. You can be sure these teams will scour the trade market for these players and try to get something back before making the non-tender official.

Projected salary: $11.1 million (team control through 2028)

Duran was a non-tender candidate even before the Jake Bauers signing pushed him out of the everyday lineup. There is no such thing as too many good players, but the Red Sox now have two first basemen (Bauers and Willson Contreras) and four outfielders (Duran, Wilyer Abreu, Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela). Mickey Gasper and Masataka Yoshida are still around too. That's eight players for five lineup spots (first base, DH, three outfield spots). On any given day, three of those guys will be on the bench. Duran, who got MVP votes in 2024, had a 20-20 season in 2026, but it came with a ballooning strikeout rate and a .266 on-base percentage. He has been on the trade block for close to two years now and the writing is on the wall. If the Red Sox are unable to trade Duran this week, there's a real chance he'll get non-tendered Friday given his hefty salary projection.

Projected salary: $7.7 million (team control through 2028)

Former No. 1 overall draft picks have been non-tendered in the past (Tim Beckham most recently), just not by the team that drafted them. Non-tendering Torkelson would be a tough look for the Tigers even though he has not developed into the impact hitter he was projected to be coming out of Arizona State. Simply put, the salary is beginning to outweigh the production. Torkelson, 27, is a 25-30 homer bat with one of the league's highest strikeout rates, middling on-base percentages, and no secondary value (defense, baserunning, etc.). That said, the Tigers do not have an obvious replacement first baseman ready to step in (Colt Keith was the backup in 2026). That, plus the fact that Torkelson has No. 1 pick pedigree, could keep him in Detroit another year.

Projected salary: $2.3 million (team control through 2029)

The American League Rookie of the Year in 2024, Gil has battled injuries and ineffectiveness in the two seasons since. The swing-and-miss rate on his fastball went from an elite 28.5% in 2024 to a below-average 18.8% in 2025 and 17.4% in 2026. Gil, 28, spent time in Triple-A this past season and the Yankees moved him into the bullpen late in the year, where the results were so-so. The salary projection is a pittance, particularly for a team with New York's payroll, though Gil is now out of minor-league options (he must pass through waivers to go to Triple-A) and doesn't have an obvious role. Because he is a pitcher and breathing, and also has a major award win in the not-too-distant past, the Yankees might be able to find a trade partner this week. If not, Gil is a definite non-tender candidate.

Projected salary: $7.6 million (team control through 2028)

A fan favorite and an All-Star this past season, Clement crashed hard in the second half, and the fact of the matter is he has a .295 on-base percentage in his three full seasons with the Blue Jays. Also, the soon-to-be 31-year-old's defensive numbers tumbled this year. Clement's contact skills are elite and he's a versatile, high-energy player. As a utility guy, he's an ace. As an everyday player, he's stretched. Clement's projected salary is hefty for a utility player, particularly one with limited offensive upside who no longer reliably catches the baseball. My guess is the Blue Jays will keep him and live with the salary, but it's not an obvious decision.

Projected salary: $5.1 million (team control through 2028)

Similar to Torkelson, non-tendering a former No. 1 overall pick would be a tough look for the Twins, but a clean break might be best for all involved at this point. Lewis, 27, has trended down since his boffo second half in 2023, enough that he was sent to Triple-A for a spell this summer. He's also moved down the defensive spectrum from third base to first base. It's not due to a lack of effort; Lewis is a major tinkerer who has tried all sorts of swing adjustments. It just hasn't come together. A fresh start elsewhere, away from the spotlight of former No. 1 pick and face of the franchise, might be best for him. The budget-conscious Twins could then reallocate the projected $5.1 million elsewhere on the roster. Right now, they can't count on Lewis to hit or have a meaningful impact defensively.

Projected salary: $3.4 million (team control through 2028)

In 2023, Gorman slugged 27 home runs and looked like one of baseball's top young power hitters. In the three seasons since, he has not come close to repeating that success. The hope was that moving him to third base, his natural position, would unlock Gorman's offense following the Nolan Arenado trade. That didn't happen, and Gorman spent a big chunk of the summer in Triple-A, where he continued to have a hard time making contact. Now 26, Gorman has a minor-league option remaining and can go to Triple-A again in 2027, but the signs are not subtle. The Cardinals are reportedly seeking a stopgap third baseman until top prospect Jesús Báez is ready, which would likely not be the case if they had any belief in Gorman. That projected $3.4 million salary is a high price for a reclamation project ticketed for the minors.

Projected salary: $6.9 million (team control through 2028)

Right-handed power is in short supply throughout baseball and Burger, 31 in April, has hit at least 28 home runs in three of the last four years. He is a one-tool player, though. The home runs come with low batting averages, low on-base percentages, higher-than-average strikeout rates, and little to no defensive or baserunning value. Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young said his team lacked "grit and toughness," whatever that means, and indicated he wants more hitters who grind out at-bats. That's not Burger, who can hit the ball a mile but is not known for making life tough on pitchers. The $6.9 million projection could be deemed too pricey for a player with such a limited skill set.

Projected salary: $6.6 million (team control through 2027)

Doval went from the Yankees to the Pirates at the trade deadline, then from the Pirates to the Giants on waivers in September. He's a former All-Star who led the National League in saves in 2023, two things that have boosted his arbitration salaries. Since 2023, Doval has been a middle reliever who was on the outside of the Circle of Trust™ more often than not. The 29-year-old righty still throws very hard. There's nothing wrong with his arm. It's hard to believe he gets hit as hard as he does sometimes. Doval earned $6.1 million in 2026 and a player cannot have a salary cut by more than 20% during his team control years. That would set Doval's minimum 2027 salary at $4.88 million. I wonder if the Giants would offer him a pay cut, say $5.5M or so, and tell him it's either that or a non-tender. That happens a few times a year around the league.

Projected salary: $6.5 million (team control through 2027)

A fan favorite in San Diego -- "Ho-ly Sheets!" chants are commonplace during his at-bats at Petco Park -- Sheets has fallen by the wayside a bit with the Padres, so much so that he started just one of their six postseason games this year. The 30-year-old is a platoon player who is good against righties more than great and is a defensive liability at both first base and left field. Realistically, Sheets is a platoon DH, and teams rarely pay well for that role unless they're confident they will get big offensive numbers. In the grand scheme of things, the projected $6.5 million isn't much. It is top-of-the-market dollars for this skill set, however.

Projected salary: $1.4 million (team control through 2029)

Two years ago, Blanco threw a no-hitter in his eighth career start. This year, he was so far out of the picture that he pitched once in Houston's last 12 games (two innings at the end of a 13-2 blowout), and the Astros opted to start Peter Lambert on two days' rest with a postseason spot on the line in Game 162. Blanco, who is older than you may realize (he turned 33 in August), returned from Tommy John surgery this summer and had a rough go of it. The pitching-needy Astros could send him to Triple-A next season, as he has a minor-league option remaining, but his stuff was diminished after surgery, and again, they didn't trust him late in the year. You would be surprised at how many cheap pitchers get non-tendered every year. Blanco could join them this week.

#2639. Brewers bash champion Dodgers to brink of NLCS sweep; CBS Sports Preseason All-America team revealed

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2637. 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame ballot released: 8 things to know, including newcomers, trends and a prediction

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers.

The full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman. Newcomers to the ballot are in bold.

As a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class. Those who get at least 5% of the vote can remain on the ballot the following year, and so on, for a maximum of 10 voting cycles. Players who are on the ballot for 10 years without getting 75% of the vote, in addition to players not getting 5% of the vote, fall off the ballot in ensuing years, though that doesn't mean the doors to the Hall are permanently shut.

The results will be announced on Jan. 19, with the induction set for Cooperstown over the summer.

Here's everything else you need to know about the Baseball Hall of Fame this offseason.

As alluded to earlier, there are two different votes each offseason. The BBWAA vote is for former players who have been retired from Major League Baseball for at least five years. It's the most common method in mainstream Hall of Fame ballot discussions. When you hear stuff like "first-ballot Hall of Famer," it means via the BBWAA vote.

Players who don't make it via the BBWAA vote can get extra chances via committees. That's how, for example, Jeff Kent made it last year. Formerly called the Veterans Committee, the Hall of Fame now uses Era Committees, which are divided into two categories: contemporary baseball (1980 to present) and classic (prior to 1980). The contemporary ballot is then split into two, one for players and one for non-players like umpires, executives, pioneers and managers.

Sure enough, this time around, it is a non-player Contemporary Baseball Committee, which looks at "managers, umpires and executives whose most significant career impact was realized since 1980."

We'll dive further into this group as we get closer to the Dec. 6 vote.

Giants legend Buster Posey joins the ballot, and he's one of those cases where I don't think a bunch of people need to delve deeply into his numbers. More than statistics, sometimes we get "feel" guys, as in, you just know he's a Hall of Famer. Posey qualifies there, I would think, for 75% of the electorate. We'll obviously do a deeper dive in the coming weeks, but even without the longevity component (Posey only played in parts of 12 MLB seasons), I think he's in.

As for the rest of the first-timers, the best case would be Jon Lester. Given the way a lot of similar starting pitchers have been treated in voting in recent years, my hunch is he'll be able to hang around on the ballot, but he has a major uphill battle in order to get in.

Then you're looking at Brett Gardner, Ryan Zimmerman, Kyle Seager, the short peak of Jake Arrieta and relief work of Andrew Miller. Good players worth mentioning, of course, but they won't sniff the Hall and it seems likely all behind Posey and Lester are one-and-dones on this ballot, as they'll fall short of 5% of the vote.

This is the sixth year for Alex Rodriguez on the ballot, which means it's the sixth time that I point out that we don't really need much time to go over his case. His numbers say he's one of the 10 best position players of all time, but his ties to PEDs are keeping him out to this point.

He did rise from 37.1% of the vote in 2025 to 40% last time, a new high-water mark. The progress is too modest to believe it's trending toward him getting in, but the number this year is certainly worth watching. If he somehow makes a leap to the 50% range, a deeper conversation might be in order.

While some voters don't mind sending in blank ballots to prove some sort of nebulous point, most impose limits on themselves. Whether it's the actual rule of 10 or some voters saying they'll only vote, for example, for a maximum of three players on any given ballot, relatively weak ballots can leave openings for the best players to show huge gains. With Carlos Beltràn and Andruw Jones getting in last year and only one strong first-year candidate, perhaps Chase Utley can benefit.

Utley is only in his fourth year on the ballot, but he's already made significant gains:

He only needs to add 15.9 points after jumping nearly 20 last voting cycle. The situation is ripe for Utley to either get all the way in or get close enough to where he probably makes the Hall of Fame in 2028.

Some of us are pushing to lower the Hall of Fame standard on modern starting pitchers, given the decreases in workload and how it affects their career numbers. We might be making some headway, but it's still tough sledding. Here are the holdover starting pitchers and their standing:

The bar for relievers to make the Hall of Fame is justly pretty high. We recently saw Billy Wagner make a late move and make it in his last try on the BBWAA ballot. Francisco Rodríguez has had four chances on the ballot and gotten between 7.8% and 11.8% of the vote thus far.

K-Rod ranks sixth all time in saves and has good rate stats. He's worth tracking as it relates to three active relievers. Kenley Jansen is third in saves with a similar number of innings pitched to K-Rod. Craig Kimbrel is fifth and has more than 100 fewer innings pitched. Aroldis Chapman is ninth and in the ballpark of Kimbrel in workload to this point.

If K-Rod continues to have trouble making headway toward induction, does that mean Kimbrel and Chapman will have trouble as well? What about Jansen?

Who else is back on the ballot? A quick look:

Posey is a lock. If the committee era chooses Bochy, Baker and/or Sabean, that would be some nice San Francisco flavor, too, right? I'll predict that committee ballot at a later date, though.

I'll also say Utley's good roll here continues with a relatively weak ballot (at least when you factor in what the PED stain has done to some guys).

On the player side, my 2027 Hall of Fame class prediction is Buster Posey and Chase Utley.

#2633. MLB rumors: Orioles narrow down search in hunt for starting pitchers; reliever market heating up

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving. In Major League Baseball, that usually means a slow news week. Those of us wanting a flurry of moves before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 are starting to lose a little hope, but hey, it's still possible. We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition.

As for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov. 16, let's go.

The Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner. They have extended a qualifying offer to Trevor Rogers and though he's expected to decline it, a reunion remains possible. If not, the Orioles are also reportedly interested in lefty free agents Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd and David Peterson.

Rogers is the best option here. He finished last season with a 2.90 ERA in his last 20 starts. CBS Sports ranked him as the No. 3 free agent this offseason and the best non-Tarik Skubal pitcher on the market. Here's part of the write-up:

Rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years.

As things stand, the Orioles' rotation starts with right-handers Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Cade Povich is a left-handed option, but they'd clearly like someone else who could qualify as a frontline starter from the left-handed side.

Former Cy Young winner Sandy Alcantara has been involved in trade rumors for years and the Marlins never end up moving him. More of the same this offseason? Probably.

"I expect Sandy to be on the Marlins next year," general manager Peter Bendix told MLB Network.

Alcantara, 31, was 13-11 with a 3.87 ERA, 1.23 WHIP and 153 strikeouts in an MLB-best 214 innings last season. He also grabbed three saves down the stretch as the Marlins started experimenting with using starters in relief on their bullpen day between starts. The 2022 Cy Young winner missed all of 2024 after having Tommy John surgery and started to show flashes of his old self last season. He's now making $21 million in 2027 before hitting free agency.

If the Marlins contend, he'll surely stay put, but if they fall out of contention, it'll be another round of trade rumors.

Free agent left-hander A.J. Minter is getting a lot of interest, per MLB Network. Coming off a season in which he was productive for both the Mets and Twins (in all, a 2.56 ERA, 1.05 WHIP and 41 strikeouts in 45 ⅔ innings), he's being chased by at least the Blue Jays, Nationals, Phillies, Rangers and Royals.

Though he's closed on occasion, Minter has been a quality setup man for most of his 10 MLB years, especially with the Braves in the 2020-24 range. He has good playoff numbers, too, with a 2.88 ERA in 20 career postseason appearances.

The Brewers have acquired right-handed reliever Ryan Walker from the Giants for two minor-league pitchers, the team announced late Sunday. Walker, 30, was up and down in his four years with the Giants, which included time as a closer. He had a 1.91 ERA, 10 saves and 2.8 WAR in 2024, but lost the job of closer during a sub-par 2025 season. Last year, he pitched to a 7.16 ERA and 1.81 WHIP in 32 ⅔ innings.

We have plenty of examples of the Brewers buying low on a player and ending up getting the best version of him, so Walker is the latest to keep an eye on here.
